full_judgment: 16. Now we will take up the case of M/s Haque Brothers (Industries) Ltd and M/s Haque Brothers (Carbide) Ltd so far it relates to the subscription of increases share capital. In Company Appeal Nos. 6 and 7 of 1985 it has been stated by the present Respondent No. 1 that on search of the record of the Company at the Office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies, Dhaka further allotment of shares were found in favour of Mr Tamizul Haque and his wife on 27-12-78. It is asserted that this allotment of shares was made without any extra-ordinary General Meeting of the Company held for the purpose and without any resolution increasing the capital of the Company and as such the allotment of shares as shown in the subsequent returns are wholly illegal, void and fraudulent. It has also been asserted that notices for such allotment of new shares were never served on the respondent No. 1 and the entire matter is liable to be rejected as fraudulent. In Affidavit-in-opposition it has been stated that notices were served on respondent No. 1 and the copy of the notices along with certificate of posting Annexure 'H' and H(I) has been filed by appellant No. 2 in this case. Exhibit 'H' is an offer of further issue of capital as contemplated in section 105C of the Companies Act. The respondent No. 1's case is that the allotment of shares was made without any extra-ordinary General meeting of the Company and without any resolution increasing the capital of the Company PW2 Mr Shamsul Huq deposed that no shares were issued to him and other shareholders and no intimation was given to him. According to this witness, this was also a fraudulent issue of share. In cross-examination he denied the receipt Exhibit 'H' when his attention was drawn to the letter dated 16-3-78 and 22-9-80. He further stated in cross-examination that he did not know that further shares were issued in these two companies because from 1977 he was never allowed to look into the Companies record. In this regard we may refer to Exhibit 7 Office Order of Mr Tamizul Haque dated 25-4-77 which in fact directs the Officers and Staffs of the Company not to allow any directors to see the Office records without any specific order from the Managing Director. Exhibit 'H' and 'H' (2) which were sent by certificate of posting and by registered post by the appellant No.2 has been denied to have been received by respondent No. 1 in his evidence before the Court. It is no doubt true that certificate of posting and Registration of notices carry with it a presumption of correctness but the same has been rebutted by the evidence on record in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are inclined to hold that the Respondent No. 1 was kept in darkness and the increased share capital was subscribed by Mr Tamizul Haque and his wife. The Company Judge in that view of the matter reduced proportionately the shares subscribed by Tamizul Haque and his wife and passed the order accordingly. To us it appears that issue of new shares by Mr Tamizul Haque was motivated by ulterior consideration and Respondent No. 1 has been able to make out a case of fraudulent transfer of shares. The Company Judge was fully justified to pass the consequential order under section 38 of the Companies Act.
